gaps.title: Spells do not travel from caster to target
gaps.detail: Every spell effect detonates at the target with no flight: no fireball arcs across, no bolt of frost leaves the caster's hand. DQV reads cast (caster glows) then travel then impact. Add an optional from:{x,y,z} to FX.play so the library can emit a small travelling head that lands at at:{} and then fires the burst, and give each damage spell a castMs so the presenter can time the message box to it.

events.note: FX.play now takes from:{x,y,z} and travelMs (default 190 ms): a comet head plus a 16-spark tail leaves the caster, and the burst is fired at the landing point when it arrives, so play returns {ms: effect+travel, peak: peak+travel, travelMs}. Verified in shots/P20-final/20-travel-inflight.png (the comet is mid-flight between the caster and monster markers) and 21-travel-impact.png (flames at the monster, caster empty), driven by __DQ.travel('fire_burst'). 24 frames, 122.2 fps, 0 errors.

Measured a real flight: FX.play with from and travelMs 900, frames at 150/350/550/750 ms put the comet head at screen x=273, 561, 929, 958 (diff vs a matched empty frame, maxDelta 477-507 of 765), and the burst then fires at the landing pad. It works, but at the default 190-260 ms the head is only about 126x70 px and lives for two frames, so a 7-frame 55 ms burst missed it entirely.

gaps.title: No screen shake or hit-stop on a big spell
gaps.detail: WEIGHT: a Kazapple lands with a flash and a ring but the camera never moves. FX cannot shake the camera (src/world/camera.js is P09 and the battle camera is P15), so add a Bus emit fx.shake {amp, ms} from the heavy effects (fire_big, lightning, level_pillar, shockwave) and a short freeze hint, then ask P09/P15 to honour it.

events.note: The asking side is built: FX now has setShake(fn) and the six heavy effects (fire_big 0.5, lightning 0.7, frost 0.3, shockwave 0.6, level_pillar 0.25, and fire_big via fire_burst) call it with {amp, ms}. install(ctx) routes it to Bus.emit('fx.shake', {amp, ms}), and __DQ.state().fx reports shakes and shakeHook. Measured in the real game: shakeHook true, shakes 4 over 9 effects (shots/P20-game-final/report.json); in the demo shakes 22 with no Bus attached and nothing throws. FX owns no camera, so ACTUALLY MOVING the view is filed under P15 (battle rig) and P09 (field camera).

The camera still never moves on a heavy spell. Measured in the running build: Bus.count('fx.shake') === 0 in the demo and there is no Bus.on('fx.shake') anywhere in src/ (grep: only fx.js emits it). FX.state().shakes climbs (17 after a pass over the library) and install() does route setShake to the Bus, so P20's asking side is real, but with nobody listening the scene camera is byte-identical before and after fire_big (demo cam {orbit:20,zoom:1,tx:0,tz:0,ty:1.4} unchanged; the dist 8.5->9.5 delta is the demo's own framing table, not a shake). MISFILED: P20 cannot close this. It needs Bus.on('fx.shake') in src/world/camera.js (P09) and src/battle/present.js (P15). Please move it.
Reassigned: screen shake and hit-stop live in src/battle/present.js, which P15 owns. Re-filed under P15.

gaps.title: showAll grid is too far out to judge the quiet effects
gaps.detail: demos/P20.html showAll puts 25 effects on a 6-wide grid at 21 units, where footstep_dust, smoke_puff, chest_sparkle and poison_bubbles are a few pixels across and cannot be judged. Give showAll a second pass that walks the grid pad by pad with the camera close, or drop the grid to 4 wide at 14 units.

events.note: Unchanged. demos/P20.html still has GRID.cols = 6 and showAll camTo(0,0,21,0). Measured from 01-gap3-showall.png: a 0.9-unit pad projects to about 72 px across at 21 units, and the quiet effects are far smaller than their pad - footstep_dust measures 30x22 px at 8.5 units, so at 21 units and scale 0.8 it is about 10 px across. In the frame footstep_dust, chest_sparkle and root_vines show nothing at all on their pads. __DQ.page(n) does give six-at-a-time close-ups, but showAll itself, the one shot a critic takes first, is still unjudgeable.

gaps.title: Fire is not fire: every burst blows out to white-yellow, no orange, no red, no outline
gaps.detail: Measured at each effect's own stated peak, 1280x720, on the demo meadow. fire_burst: of the non-grass pixels, 52 percent yellow and 48 percent white — ZERO orange and ZERO red pixels. fire_big: 62 percent yellow, 38 percent white, again zero orange and zero red. On screen it reads as a pale lemon lotus flower or a tulip, not a flame: five or six flat symmetrical petals round a blown-out white core. The palette already holds the right colours (K.fireMid is PAL.tile.light #e98657 and K.fireDeep is PAL.tile.dark #93402a) but they never survive, because sixteen additive flame quads at a 0.95 plus an additive white SHAPE.blob stack multiplicatively to white. Three fixes, all inside src/art/fx.js: (1) draw the flame cell in the atlas with a dark cel edge and a warm ramp (deep #93402a rim, #e98657 body, #ffd64a inner, white only in the smallest hottest quad) and render the body quads NON-additive so the colour holds, keeping additive only for the ember sparks; (2) cap the white core to about a quarter of the cluster's area and give it a short life so the peak frame is orange-dominant — a child should see orange in over 40 percent of the effect pixels; (3) make the tiers read apart by shape as well as size: Scorcha one small cluster, Scorchalot a cluster plus a rising column, Kascorcha a ground ring of flame plus the 25 percent warm orange full-screen wash and 4 px shake the SYSTEMS 3.1 brief asks for (the wash is currently screenFlash(PAL.tile.light, 0.2, 300), which the measurement shows arrives as a pale wash, not a warm orange one). The same root cause — additive white-out with no dark edge — is why ice, wind and buff all land as pale mint on green: fixing the atlas cells and the blend mode fixes the whole library.
